result:
480	I told you from the start

481	that what HaShem says is what I will say.

482	So see how beautifully the holy Or HaChaim explains:

483	Bilam refuted Balak's claim, for the lie is in his mouth: "I also spoke to your messengers," etc. It means:

484	"I also spoke to your messengers," etc.

485	And despite this, you reasoned and accepted, and sent to honor me,

486	and he doubled the wording: "your messengers whom you sent."

487	And it was not enough for him to say

488	"your messengers," and it is clear the matter is that they are yours.

489	By "your messengers" he meant the first messengers,

490	and by "whom you sent"

491	he meant the messengers he sent a second time.

492	And "saying":

493	"Also to your messengers whom you sent to me I spoke, saying."

494	What are these words, "I spoke, saying"?

495	"I spoke, saying" means: I did not speak these things only myself.

496	It's not that I told only them these things, but

497	I commanded them to say to you.

498	"I spoke, saying": that they should deliver you this message even

499	before I came to you.

500	And you did not tell me then: if so, stay at home.

501	Now it's understood, now we understand the argument between Balak

502	and Bilam. Now it's fun to watch them quarrel;

503	more so,

504	it gains flavor.

505	Now what does Bilam say to Balak? "And now, behold, I am

506	going to my people."

507	Note that Balak told Bilam four things:

508	"And you now,

509	flee."

510	Run, flee.

511	Yes.

512	"And you, go by yourself," I'm not sending an escort with you.

513	Escort.

514	"Your place" are four things. Bilam came to say

515	to Balak now: listen well, no problem, I don't

516	need you.

517	"And you, now, I am going."

518	"Behold,"

519	"behold" is by myself.

520	Don't send anyone.

521	I'm going, but I'm not fleeing.

522	Not fleeing. I go to my people, back to my place.

523	But the fourth thing you asked of me, the third thing,

524	which is number four, which is "flee," that I don't

525	accept.

526	I'm not fleeing. I'm going, I'm going even

527	with a Yemenite step: two steps forward, one step back.

528	You will not tell me to flee.

529	Someone told me that the Yemenite step is actually two steps

530	back, one forward, no.

531	Yes, but the Kurdish step, they told me, is two forward,

532	one back.

533	[snorts] I don't know if they were joking with me or

534	if they meant it seriously. There is a Kurdish step.

535	Okay, now to our subject.

536	Yes.

537	Now listen well. Look at the holy Or HaChaim,

538	how precise he is with the words, how he delights

539	in our Torah, gentlemen. "And now, behold, I am going" means: behold,

540	he is ready to fulfill the king's decree to go with them,

541	and he said it in the singular, corresponding to what was hinted to him in the word "lechá,"

542	as I explained; and he said "to my people," corresponding to what he said to him, "to your place."

543	But as for the detail of fleeing,

544	he did not inform him.

545	Calm down, relax.

546	[snorts] For they did not fear him. Bilam is not afraid

547	of Balak, for he was a great sorcerer. "Go and learn how much they struggled

548	with him, Bnei Yisrael, until his death." That is, says

549	the holy Or HaChaim: go learn how much they struggled

550	with him, how hard it was until they managed to kill him.

551	Where is this written? The holy Zohar, volume III, page 194,

552	side a, Parashat Pinchas.

553	"And all the more so others." So if Israel struggled with him

554	so much until they killed him, all the more so others, who

555	cannot do him harm. And he refers, gentlemen,

556	to the Zohar on Parashat Pinchas, where the whole story is written,

557	with his sons as well, Yonos and Yambros,

558	who were Bilam's sons, and how in fact

559	he pursued them in the air; Tzilia, who was of the sons of Dan.

560	And there is a long and wonderful story there

561	in the holy Zohar.

562	In any case, see. [clears throat] But now,

563	how he explains, a wonderful explanation,

564	by which alone the rest of the Parashah will be understood.

565	"And now, behold, I am going to my people.

566	Come, I will advise you

567	what this people will do to your people in the end of days."

568	And then Bilam in fact begins a new prophecy here.

569	"And he took up his parable and said: The utterance of Bilam son of Beor,

570	the utterance of the man whose eye is opened; the utterance of him who hears the words of God,

571	and knows the knowledge of the Most High, who sees the vision of Shakai, fallen, yet with open eyes.

572	I see him, but not now; I behold him, but not near.

573	A star shall step forth from Yaakov, and a scepter shall rise out of Israel," which is

574	about the King Mashiach.

575	"And shall smite the corners of Moav, and break down all the children of Seth," shall break down all

576	the nation's stock. Now see,

577	Bilam says this now to Balak.

578	And what is written after this prophecy?

579	After this prophecy it is written:

580	"And Bilam rose up,

581	and went and returned to his place,

582	and Balak also went his way."

583	"And Israel dwelt in Shittim, and the people began to commit harlotry with the daughters of Moav."

584	What is the connection?

585	Chazal say that what is written in verse 11,

586	"And now I am not going to believe you, come, I will advise you what this

587	people will do to your people in the end of days."

588	So, on the words "lechá iatzchá,"

589	it is written in Rashi:

590	"Come, I will advise you what to do, and what the

591	advice is."

592	What do you want, to harm them?

593	Their God hates licentiousness,

594	etc. "...know that Bilam gave this advice,

595	to make them stumble there in licentiousness, for it says: 'Behold, they were

596	to Bnei Yisrael through the word of Bilam.'"

597	So this is in fact:

598	I am going to advise you how to make them stumble, but how

599	does this fit with the rest of the verse, "come, I will advise you what this people will do"?
